title: The Scale of a Claim
hypothesis: Changing only the lower axis bound can make framing inspectable while retaining constant data and an optional fixed reference.
selectionMethod: Internal judgments 1–5: originality, visual necessity, interaction meaning, feasibility. Not research results or public scores.

hypotheses.idea: Adjust the lower bound of one line chart
hypotheses.reason: One controlled geometric variable; exact invariant data and a direct counter-view. Selected.

hypotheses.idea: Reveal a crop's omitted surrounding evidence
hypotheses.reason: Strong counterfactual but too close to Day005's unresolved implementation.

hypotheses.idea: Move a caption between image and margin
hypotheses.reason: Placement alone is weak evidence for comprehension.
Strong alternative, but requires explaining ratios as a second concept.

hypotheses.idea: Replace decorative certainty with an uncertainty band
hypotheses.reason: Needs a defensible uncertainty model before visual exploration.

hypotheses.idea: Change chart aspect ratio without changing data
hypotheses.reason: Strongest rejected alternative; responsive dimensions confound a single-variable comparison.

hypotheses.idea: Turn ranking into an unordered field
hypotheses.reason: Changes spatial search and ordering simultaneously.

hypotheses.idea: Reveal sample exclusions one by one
hypotheses.reason: Requires a meaningful sampling context beyond authored values.

hypotheses.idea: Keep provenance visible in an animated export
hypotheses.reason: Export infrastructure would dominate today's visual question.
Haptic hardware and accessibility testing unavailable.

challenge: If readers cannot identify unchanged values or the effect persists despite a reference, visible framing alone is insufficient. No participant result yet.
